To find the complex conjugate of a vector, we take the complex conjugate of the entries of the vector. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\overset{―}{x}}_{1} & =\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}4+3\text{i} \\ -1+3\text{i}\end{aligned}]} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{4+3\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{-1+3\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4-3\text{i} \\ -1-3\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying the second vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{i}\cdot {x}_{2} & =\text{i}\cdot [\begin{aligned}5+4\text{i} \\ -4-3\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5\text{i}+4{\text{i}}^{2} \\ -4\text{i}-3{\text{i}}^{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4+5\text{i} \\ 3-4\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\overset{―}{x}}_{1}+\text{i}\cdot {x}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}4-3\text{i} \\ -1-3\text{i}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-4+5\text{i} \\ 3-4\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2\text{i} \\ 2-7\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
